## Target outcomes

Taken from the course's `reproducibilityReport.Rmd`, which quotes the Study 1 results section:

> Only 10 of the 61 participants in the hypothetical condition chose to exchange contact information with the unattractive potential date (16%). In contrast, 26 of the 71 participants in the real condition chose to exchange contact information (37%). A chi-square test of independence indicated that participants were significantly less likely to reject the unattractive potential date in the real condition compared with the hypothetical condition, X\^2(1, N = 132) = 6.77, p = .009.

| \# | Target outcome (quoted) | Paper value(s) |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | "Only 10 of the 61 participants in the hypothetical condition chose to exchange contact information ... (16%)" | 10 / 61, 16% |
| 2 | "26 of the 71 participants in the real condition chose to exchange contact information (37%)" | 26 / 71, 37% |
| 3 | "X\^2(1, N = 132) = 6.77" | χ² = 6.77, df = 1, N = 132 |
| 4 | "p = .009" | p = .009 |

## Reproduction

The agent's code (Claude Code), copied from its completed `reproducibilityReport.Rmd`. The only change is the data path.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(haven)
```

```{r}
#| label: load
d <- read_sav("partA_data/Empathy Gap Study 1 data.sav")
```

```{r}
#| label: preprocess
# condition: 0 = hypothetical, 1 = real; exchangeinfo: 1 = yes, 2 = no (SPSS value labels)
d_tidy <- d %>%
  mutate(condition = as_factor(condition),
         exchangeinfo = as_factor(exchangeinfo)) %>%
  select(ID, condition, exchangeinfo)

nrow(d_tidy)
sum(is.na(d_tidy$condition))
sum(is.na(d_tidy$exchangeinfo))
```

```{r}
#| label: analysis
desc <- d_tidy %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(n_total = n(),
            n_exchange = sum(exchangeinfo == "yes"),
            pct_exchange = round(100 * n_exchange / n_total, 1))

kable(desc, col.names = c("Condition", "N", "N exchanged contact info", "% exchanged"))

contingency <- table(d_tidy$condition, d_tidy$exchangeinfo)
contingency

chi <- chisq.test(contingency, correct = FALSE)
chi
```

Reported in APA style: χ²(`r chi$parameter`, N = `r sum(contingency)`) = `r sprintf("%.2f", chi$statistic)`, p = `r sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", chi$p.value))`.

Agent's own claim about success, and whether it was right:

The agent reported that it was able to reproduce all of the results above, and the counts match exactly. The original authors shared a clean data file with clear instructions for analysis, so the agent shared the code was straightforward to write.

The agent was correct about successfully reproducing the results from the paper.

## Assessment

Is the primary result analytically reproducible? What would have made this take 30 minutes?

Yes, the primary result was analytically reproducible - it took no guesswork, help from the authors, and no extra steps beyond the template's hint to turn off the continuity correction.

Caveat: The paper reported 150 participants, but the data file shared had only 132 analyzed participants. The results are reproducible from the data as shared, however, it was not possible to check the exclusions that took the sample from 150 to 132.
